summary.en: Install a JDK and follow a Java source file through compilation and execution.
summary.bn: JDK বসিয়ে সোর্স কোড থেকে চলন্ত জাভা প্রোগ্রাম পর্যন্ত ধাপগুলো বুঝুন।

notes: Use a JDK 17 or 21 and target Java 17; this lesson uses the traditional main signature.

sections.title: The tools between source and execution
Choose an editor without losing the terminal picture
Separate source errors from tool errors

examples.title: A first greeting
examples.explanationHtml: The launch method prints one line. The semicolon ends the print statement.

examples.title: Two statements in order
examples.explanationHtml: The first statement prints the course code. The second creates a separate line for the lab.

examples.title: Joining printed pieces
examples.explanationHtml: print keeps the cursor on the same line. println adds a line ending after 17.

practice.title: Read a roll label
practice.statementHtml: Input: one integer roll from 1 to 999. Print Roll: followed by the roll and a newline.
hints: The plus sign joins a label and a number.

practice.title: Print a course ticket
practice.statementHtml: Input: a course number from 100 to 499. Print CSE followed by that number on the first line, then Lab ready on the second.

practice.title: Diagnose a missing compiler
practice.statementHtml: java -version works, but javac -version is not found. Give two checks before editing the program.
hints: A source error cannot explain a missing command.
practice.answerHtml: Check that a JDK, rather than only a runtime, is installed. Then check whether its bin folder appears in PATH. Open a new terminal after changing PATH and run both version commands again.

practice.title: Move compiled code
practice.statementHtml: A class compiled for Java 17 is copied to another operating system. State what the destination needs and what could still prevent it from running.
hints: Distinguish the portability of bytecode from the portability of a native library.
practice.answerHtml: The destination needs a compatible Java runtime, version 17 or newer. The JVM must match the destination platform. Missing external libraries, native dependencies or incorrect classpath settings can still prevent execution.

quiz.prompt: Which line ending does println add to this greeting?
quiz.explanation: println prints the text inside the quotes and ends the line.

quiz.prompt: How do print and println combine the lab label?
quiz.explanation: print preserves the space after Lab and does not end the line.

quiz.prompt: In which order do the two launch statements appear?
quiz.explanation: Statements in main execute from top to bottom.
The development kit contains javac. A runtime alone may lack development tools.

quiz.prompt: What does the JVM consume during a normal class launch?
quiz.explanation: javac creates bytecode. The JVM loads and executes that bytecode.

quiz.prompt: Which terminal command launches Main.class from the current classpath?
quiz.explanation: The launcher receives a class name. javac is the compiler command.

quiz.prompt: Why might javac reject public class Main inside Ticket.java?
options: The public top-level class name must match the filename
The source needs a C header
quiz.explanation: A public Main class belongs in Main.java. The class used here has package access but follows the same teaching filename.

quiz.prompt: What should you configure in IntelliJ IDEA, VS Code or NetBeans before running?
quiz.explanation: An IDE invokes Java tools using its configured JDK and language level.

quiz.prompt: Can Java 17 run bytecode that requires Java 21?
options: No; use a compatible newer runtime or compile for 17
Yes, if the source is renamed
quiz.explanation: Bytecode has a version. A runtime cannot generally load classes requiring a later version.

quiz.prompt: What is the useful meaning of platform independence?
options: One JVM executable runs on every CPU
Compatible JVMs can execute the same portable bytecode
Every operating system has identical paths
quiz.explanation: The JVM implementation is platform-specific. Portable bytecode sits above that difference.

keyPoints.en: The JDK includes the compiler and runtime tools.
keyPoints.bn: JDK-তে কম্পাইলার আর প্রোগ্রাম চালানোর টুল থাকে।

keyPoints.en: javac turns source code into class files.
keyPoints.bn: javac সোর্স কোড থেকে ক্লাস ফাইল বানায়।

keyPoints.en: java Main launches the class named Main.
keyPoints.bn: java Main লিখলে Main নামের ক্লাস চালু হয়।

keyPoints.en: An IDE still needs a configured JDK.
keyPoints.bn: IDE ব্যবহার করলেও সঠিক JDK দেখিয়ে দিতে হয়।

examQuestions.question: Differentiate JDK, JRE and JVM.
examQuestions.answerHtml: JDK supplies development tools plus a runtime. JRE means the runtime environment and libraries; modern distributions may package it differently. JVM is the engine that executes bytecode.

examQuestions.question: Show the terminal path from Main.java to printed text.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Save the source as Main.java. Run javac --release 17 Main.java to create Main.class. Run java Main from the classpath root. javac reports source problems; java reports launch or runtime problems.

examQuestions.question: Explain why moving a class file does not require moving a Windows JVM to Linux.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The class file contains portable bytecode. Linux uses its own JVM implementation to execute that bytecode. The runtime must support the class file version.
